title: Longitudinal prediction of adolescent depression from environmental and polygenic risk scores
title_zh: 基于环境和多基因风险评分的青少年抑郁纵向预测
abstract: Abstract Understanding adolescent depression risk is vital for mitigating its long-term adverse effects. Though polygenic risk scores (PRS) explain increasing proportions of heritable risk, environmental risk remains challenging to quantify, hindering prediction. Existing prediction models often examine environmental risk in isolation, and vary in the number of predictors examined (between 8–800 + ), limiting generalisability. Here, we develop a model predicting adolescent depression symptoms (depRS) from a review of key environmental risk factors and assess depRS and PRS prediction of major depressive disorder (MDD) at 2-year follow-up. Using data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study (N = 9 797; 47% female), we generated PRS in European, African, American Admixed and East Asian ancestries from a recent trans-ancestry genome-wide study of MDD. We trained depRS to predict parent-reported depression symptoms at 2-year follow-up (age 11–13) from baseline predictors (age 9–11), using Elastic Net regression with 10-fold cross-validation for variable selection. The final depRS model included 12 predictors and explained 12.3% of overall variance. Parental depression, witnessing domestic violence, sleep duration and dieting emerged as top predictors of depression symptoms. depRS showed better-than-chance classification of parent- (AUC = 0.69 [0.66–0.73]) and youth self-reported MDD (AUC = 0.67 [0.64–0.71]), outperforming PRS classification of parent-reported MDD (AUC = 0.64 [0.60–0.68]). Combining depRS and PRS maximised accuracy for both outcomes (Parent AUC = 0.71 [0.68–0.75]; Youth AUC = 0.70 [0.66–0.73]). Though external validation of depRS across geographically and gender diverse cohorts is needed to assess generalisability, findings highlight sleep and dieting as potential targets for mitigating risk and demonstrate the utility of genetic scores in models predicting adolescent depression.
abstract_zh: 理解青少年抑郁风险对于减轻其长期不良影响至关重要。虽然多基因风险评分（PRS）能解释不断增加的遗传风险比例，但环境风险的量化仍然具有挑战性，阻碍了预测能力。现有的预测模型往往单独考察环境风险，且考察预测因子数量差异巨大（在8–800+个之间），这限制了其普适性。本研究旨在通过回顾关键环境风险因子，构建一个预测青少年抑郁症状（depRS）的模型，并评估depRS和PRS在2年随访中对重度抑郁障碍（MDD）的预测能力。利用青少年脑力认知发展（ABCD）研究的数据（N = 9 797；47% 女性），我们基于最近一项跨祖先基因组-wide研究的结果，在欧洲、非洲、美洲混血和东亚祖先中生成了MDD的PRS。我们利用弹性网络回归配合10折交叉验证，从基线预测因子（9–11岁）出发，预测2年随访（11–13岁）的父母报告的抑郁症状。最终的depRS模型包含12个预测因子，解释了总体变异的12.3%。父母抑郁、目睹家庭暴力、睡眠时长和节食被确定为抑郁症状的主要预测因子。depRS在父母报告（AUC = 0.69 [0.66–0.73]）和青少年自述（AUC = 0.67 [0.64–0.71]）的MDD分类上均优于机遇水平，且优于PRS对父母报告MDD的分类（AUC = 0.64 [0.60–0.68]）。depRS与PRS的结合最大化了两种结果的准确性（父母AUC = 0.71 [0.68–0.75]；青少年AUC = 0.70 [0.66–0.73]）。尽管需要对depRS进行外部验证，以评估其在地理和性别多样性队列中的普适性，但研究结果突出了睡眠和节食作为降低风险的潜在目标，并展示了遗传评分在预测青少年抑郁中的实用性。
